Abram returned from Egypt, rich in livestock, silver, and gold.
Lot also had flocks and tents, and the land could not hold them both.
Abram said to Lot: let there be no strife between us, for we are family.
The whole land is before you. If you go left, I will go right.
Lot saw the Jordan plain, well watered like the garden of the Lord.
He chose it, and pitched his tent near Sodom.
Now the people of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against the Lord.
After Lot left, the Lord told Abram: look in every direction.
All the land you see, I will give to you and your descendants forever.
They will be like the dust of the earth.
Abram settled at the oaks of Mamre, and built an altar to the Lord.
Abram let Lot choose first, to keep the peace.
Lot chose by what looked good. Abram trusted what God had promised.
Peace is worth more than winning, and trust is worth more than what we can see.
Today, choose peace over being right.
What would you give up to keep the peace?
